payload.description:
## Context
Measured on 2026-11-11 with Claude Code 2.1.322 and a scratch probe mod in tmux. A ui.render tree whose Text child holds a control character of class Cc other than tab and newline is refused whole: the engine skips the hook with the line 'ui.render hook skipped: returned the wrong shape (a tree AbovePrompt refuses: a text child holds a control character (an escape sequence))'. So no escape sequence reaches the terminal. A bidi override U+202E draws as U+FFFD, a zero width space draws as nothing visible, a tab expands, and a newline breaks the line. The engine types say the same for Text and Code: tab and newline are their only control characters.
The fold path of simple-view already escapes these characters through shownLine in fold.ts. The row label paths do not: bashLabel in register.ts with the description and commandLabel, programOf in command.ts, the Grep and Glob pattern in searchTarget in reading.ts, and every file path through shownPath in output.ts. A label that holds such a character, such as a carriage return or an escape in a command, a pattern or a file name, makes the engine refuse the simple row, so the engine draws its own row and logs a skip line.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
When the board body is 41 columns or more on the terminal, the Session, Tasks and Agents sections each draw in a rounded text frame in their role key (Session claude, Tasks planMode, Agents merged), with the section title on the top edge. Below 41 columns, inline above the prompt and on the desktop app, no frame draws, and each title draws bold in its role key.
When the context percent is known, the Session section shows a ten-cell gauge and the percent, and the 5 hour and 7 day limits show five-cell gauges with their percents. A gauge rounds down and the percent always prints. At 80 percent or more the gauge and the percent draw in warning, with the word high.
When permission checks have run, the Session section shows one cell for each of the last 20 checks, oldest first: a filled bar for allowed in success, a hollow bar for asked in permission, a filled square for denied in error. It shows the counts of the file family, the shell family and every other tool, and when a denied check is among the last 20 the words 1 denied in error replace the counts. /board stats lists the same verdicts as words.
When a main-loop request starts, the Session section shows the model id without a leading claude-, the effort of that request and the permission mode from the latest classic SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit or Stop event. A part with no source is left out and never guessed.
When a turn runs, the Session section shows the turn duration, the edits, the errors and the cost added. When the session is idle, the same row shows the last turn dim.
When the person opens a subagent row, the board shows the last 3 tool calls of that agent, each with a mark for its outcome and its age, and, once the agent has ended, the first line of its answer. Credentials are masked as in the checks.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
When a folder holds a changed file, its name draws in the key of its strongest state: error for U or D, else warning for M or R, else success for A or untracked.
When git status changes, the mod runs one git --no-optional-locks diff --numstat -z HEAD call for that change, after the status call. Each changed file and folder shows its added lines as +N in success and its removed lines as -N in error, both always printed. A binary file shows bin, and an untracked file shows no count.
When the numstat call fails or times out, the tree stays, no line count shows, and a dim note at the foot names the exit or the timeout. After two slow runs the call is skipped, and the note says so.
When the branch is ahead of its upstream, the ahead count draws in success, and a behind count draws in warning. When an upstream exists, the header shows its name dim, read from the branch.upstream line of the same status call.
When the body is under 41 columns, the line counts and the totals drop and the colours stay. Inline above the prompt, the upstream name drops.

payload.title: board: an answer press reaches Claude at once, tasks for you show in full, and /board opens one pane

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context

Owner feedback of 2026-11-17, his words condensed: (1) he rarely uses the board, it takes too much space; (2) the board opens two boards, so closing it takes two closes; (3) tasks assigned to him that he can answer are not readable, he sees only their start; (4) choosing an option is not given to the agent; it should go to the agent through the API, or at least be pasted into the chat for Enter, or better be sent automatically on the press.

Facts (plan review agent): showPane in mods/handily-board/hooks/board.ts:71-79 always opens both panes tasks and sessions (board.ts:10), shown as two tabs; /board close closes both (board.ts:87-91) but a close from the tab closes one. For you rows cut the title with fitted(title, room) at hooks/for-you-view.ts:122 and each decide option to 20 columns (OPTION_COLUMNS, line 17 and 255); only 3 open tasks show before +N more (OPEN_SHOWN). The README says an answer reaches Claude with the next prompt (README.md:417). Engine API: $.prompt.submit (index.d.ts:3153, asUser at 9977) and $.prompt.fill (3191); a plugin submit skips its own prompt.submit hook (3146).

Decisions: council 2026-11-17, submit-now 2 of 3 (dissent safety: a misclick starts a turn); guard from the Orchestrator: after a press the board shows the exact text it sent.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When the person presses a decide option or Send on an answer task, the board submits the answer as the person prompt at once, or when the session is idle, and shows the exact text it sent.
- When a task for the person has a long title, question or options, the rows wrap the whole text at 40 and 120 columns instead of cutting it.
- When the person runs /board, the board opens one pane, and one close closes it.

payload.text: [conversation 2026-11-17] Owner plan with the handily session: the board lane takes feedback 2, 3 and 4 together, because all three touch the same board files. Council on how a press reaches Claude: submit-now 2 of 3 (user, skeptic), dissent safety (fill-for-enter). payload.description:
## Trigger

When a session runs subagents in the background, I want one pane that shows what each subagent does now, so I can follow the lanes without opening each transcript.

## Notes (2026-10-08)

- The user wants this beside session-board, not in its place. session-board shows the sessions of the machine; this view shows the subagents inside one session.
- The engine gives the rows: $.agent.list() has id, description, type, status and parentId per agent; tool.call events carry agentId, so a mod can show the current tool, a tool count and the elapsed time per subagent.
- Open: a new mod, or a second view of session-board, or an extension of the engine's own background agent view. Decide in the design with a second opinion.

## Scope

- mods/agent-board/ or mods/session-board/
- .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
- docs/design.md
- docs/mocks.md
payload.requirements: - User request 2026-10-08: a subagent (background session) board in addition to the session pane.
payload.title: agent-board: a pane that shows what each subagent of this session does

payload.text: Design 2026-10-08: design lane plus Codex second opinion, both pick a new mod agent-board with its own Pane. Confirmed in the types: tool.call input carries the agentId of a subagent loop; agent.spawn fires for the Agent tool and resolves with an optional agentId; turn.complete carries durationMs and an optional usage; agent.list leaves out workflow agents and drops ended agents; no render component reaches the engine tasks list. Limits: two Panes do not show at once, they become tabs; agent.list history expires, so the mod keeps the rows it saw and marks lost history as unknown; forked-skill agents may appear without agent.spawn. Hot path: the tool.call hook passes main-loop calls straight through and keeps bounded memory per agent; list and render work runs only while the pane is shown. Live probes open: tool.call with agentId from a background subagent, agent.list retention, the hook cost.

Live probe 2026-10-08 (Claude Code 2.1.294): P4 tool.call of a subagent carries agentId, main-loop calls carry none; two agent ids appeared in tool.call that agent.list never showed (source unknown, likely plugin or forked loops), so the board must accept unknown ids. P5 agent.spawn resolved with model and agentId; agent.list showed the Explore agent running, then completed, and still listed it 90 s after the spawn; parentId absent for a main-loop spawn.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When /agent-board runs, the mod shall open the pane agent-board, and the pane shall show one row per subagent that agent.list returns or that tool.call showed.
- While no subagent exists, the pane shall show No subagents in this session yet.
- When a tool.call with an agentId starts, the row of that agent shall show the tool and its target; when the call resolves, the row shall add 1 to its tool count.
- When a tool.call has no agentId, the mod shall pass it on unchanged and change no row.
- If a hook of the mod throws, then the tool call shall still resolve with the result of next.
- While the pane is shown, the mod shall redraw every second and show the elapsed time since the spawn; when the pane closes, the timer shall stop.
- When a subagent has a parentId, its row shall show under and the parent name or description.
- While every subagent is completed, failed or killed, the header shall read all N done, and the rows shall keep their tool count and time.

payload.text: Agreement 2026-10-08 (user and main session): the work is the agent-board mod with its own Pane, a tab beside session-board, built from agent.list, agent.spawn, tool.call with agentId and turn.complete. Done means the acceptance criteria hold, a correctness review passed, and npm run check passes on main.

- When the 5 hour usage rises, the Session line shows the projected time to 100 percent.
- When the usage crosses 80 or 95 percent, every session of this machine shows one warning per cycle, not one per session.
payload.description:
## Context

The Session line projects when the 5 hour and the weekly limits reach 100 percent, from the slope of the recent readings. It warns once per cycle at 80 and 95 percent, shared across the sessions of this machine.

Reference: limit-watch (MIT). Source: survey of github.com/karanb192/awesome-claude-code-mods and its reference mods on 2026-10-28. Clones were read only. handily copies no code and adds no dependency.
payload.title: board: a pace projection for the usage limits

payload.text: [mocks proposed 2026-11-12] Designer mocks, sent to the Development session for approval. Source today: readUsage in register.tsx calls $.session.usage().rateLimits into withUsage in vitals.ts, and session.measure goes through withMeasure and limitsAfter; each limit is kind, percentUsed and an optional resetsAt; vitals keep only the latest reading, so the build adds a list of readings per kind, dropped when resetsAt changes or the percent falls. The line shows full ~1h only when 100 percent comes before resetsAt; it shows nothing with fewer than 2 readings, less than 15 minutes of readings, flat or falling use, or a last reading over 30 minutes old; with no rateLimits the details read limits: none reported. No invented number. Store key per kind limit-warned:five_hour with v 1, kind, cycle as resetsAt, level 80 or 95, at and by session id; with no compare-and-set a session writes, waits 200 to 800 ms, reads back and toasts only if by is still its own; a past resetsAt or a cycle more than 10 minutes apart is stale and deleted as in sessions.ts deleteExpired. Toast: 5h limit at 80% then full ~1h at this pace and resets in 2h. Open questions: which session toasts, first claimer recommended, taste; tilde before the time, yes per 8.14c; the toast mark, taste. Known limit: two sessions that pass the read-back together both warn.

[decision 2026-11-12] Decided by the orchestrator, 2026-11-12: Q1 yes, an edit between failures; Q2 yes, retry rows first among running agents in the band; Q3 yes, 1 retry in the Agents head; Q5 yes, a tilde before the projected time. For now and open to the owner: Q4 the first session that claims the key shows the toast; Q6 the mark ◆ with a word for 95 percent, not a colour; the mark and the level word are constants in one place. Conditions: the retry row never shows a secret, using the board mask for commands or else only the first word, with a test of a command that carries a token; the pace record states the known limit that two sessions can both warn, with tests for each nothing-shows case and for limits: none reported.
[owner answer 2026-11-12] Relayed by the Development session: the owner confirmed Q4, the first session that claims the key shows the toast, and Q6, the mark ◆ with a word for 95 percent.

When the 5 hour or weekly usage rises over at least 15 minutes of readings and reaches 100 percent before its reset at that pace, the Session line shows full with a tilde and the projected time, such as full ~1h, as the mocks recorded on this record on 2026-11-12.
When there are fewer than 2 readings, less than 15 minutes of readings, flat or falling use, or a last reading over 30 minutes old, the Session line shows no projection, and when Claude Code reports no limits the details read limits: none reported; no number is invented.

- If simple-view writes a mode value other than on or off, a test shall fail.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When simple-view changes the values of its mode state, I want a quiet-items test to fail, so I can trust that /simple off still turns the quiet rows off.

## Evidence

- mods/quiet-items/hooks/register.tsx reads the state simple-view.mode as unknown and compares it to the string off.
- mods/simple-view/hooks/register.ts writes the mode on or off.
- mods/quiet-items/quiet-items.test.ts replaces simple-view with a fake plugin that writes the mode, so a change in the real producer fails no test.

## Scope

- mods/quiet-items/quiet-items.test.ts
- mods/simple-view/simple-view.test.ts
- mods/simple-view/types/
- mods/quiet-items/hooks/register.tsx
payload.requirements: - User decision 2026-10-08 (go on the ranked plan): a change to the producer of the mode must not break /simple off without a failing test.

- The README describes the pane as built, the version is 0.4.0, and npm run check passes.

- mods/task-pane/README.md
- mods/task-pane/types/*
- mods/task-pane/.claude-plugin/plugin.json

claude plugin test mods/task-pane and npm run check; the main session runs a live check on tmux -L handily-live on this Team account: Claude works with and without a list, and one subagent runs.

payload.description:
## Context

When the fourth review of handily-ntinw.1 ran on 2026-11-01, a resumed agent whose run ended only through the agent list, with no turn.complete and with the same ended status as before, stayed running on the board while the Log said done. The board reads the list every 10 s and only while the pane is shown. Whether the engine ends a resumed subagent with no turn.complete is not known. Measure it live first, then fix from that fact.
payload.title: board: a resumed agent that ends with no turn end leaves the running state

payload.text: [measurement 2026-11-11] Claude Code 2.1.322, tmux session with a scratch probe mod that logs turn.start, turn.complete and agent.spawn with agentId, and samples the agent list every 1 s. 4 resumed runs in 3 shapes: SendMessage to an ended background Explore agent, twice; SendMessage to a general-purpose agent while it ran, which then waited on its own background shell and was woken by the shell notification. The Agent tool had no foreground option, so no foreground agent ran. RESULT: every resumed run got turn.start and turn.complete with its agentId and reason answer. No run ended through the list alone. EVENT ORDER of a resume: list completed; turn.start for the agent with the message text; agent.spawn result with the same agentId about 30 ms later; list running within 1 s; turn.start of the main loop with the hand-back about 50 ms before turn.complete for the agent; list completed within 1 s. A run that waits on its own shell gets turn.complete while the list says waiting; the wake gives a new turn.start and a new agent.spawn result, and the list goes waiting to running to completed. NOT SEEN: a resumed run with no turn.complete. The code path stays a defect: withRunStart sets endedAt to null, and isListedEnd in agents.ts and noteListedEnds in register.tsx count an end only when the listed status changes, so a run whose running status the 10 s list read misses stays running when no turn.complete comes.
